common.copyFailed: Copying failed. Select the text and copy it manually.
common.name: Name
common.networkError: Aether could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again.
common.httpError: The server responded with status {status}. Try again in a moment.
common.invalidAddress: {value} is not a valid email address.
common.invalidAddressOrDomain: {value} is not a valid email address or @domain.

login.title: Sign in
login.defaultMessage: Sign in to read your mail and manage your organization.
login.noMethodConfigured: No sign-in method is configured on this installation. Ask the operator to enable password sign-in or add an identity provider.

errors.rate_limited: Too many sign-in attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.unknown_provider: That sign-in provider is not available. Choose another sign-in method.
errors.provider_unavailable: The identity provider could not be reached. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.provider_denied: The identity provider did not approve the sign-in. Try again, or contact your administrator.
errors.state_mismatch: The sign-in request could not be matched to this browser. Start the sign-in again from this page.
errors.state_expired: The sign-in request expired. Start the sign-in again.
errors.exchange_failed: Aether could not complete the sign-in with the identity provider. Try again.
errors.invalid_token: The identity provider returned an invalid response. Contact your administrator.
errors.email_unverified: Your identity provider has not verified your email address. Verify it there, then try again.
errors.not_provisioned: Your account does not have access to Aether yet. Ask your administrator to add you.
errors.account_disabled: This account is suspended. Contact your administrator.
errors.limit_reached: Your organization has reached its mailbox or storage limit, so a mailbox could not be created for you. Ask your administrator.
errors.shared_mailbox: This address is a shared mailbox and cannot sign in. Sign in with your own account; the shared mailbox appears in your sidebar once an administrator adds you.
errors.fallback: Sign-in failed ({code}). Try again, or contact your administrator.

mail.noMailboxTitle: You do not have a mailbox yet
mail.noMailboxDescription: An administrator creates mailboxes in Administration. Once one is assigned to your account it appears here.
mail.forwardedAttachmentsOmitted: Forwarded attachments can't be sent from {address}, so they were left out.

folders.readOnlyNotice: Read only. You can read this mailbox but not send, move, or delete.
folders.foldersLoadError: The folders could not be loaded.

dialog.deleteWithMessages: Its {messages} will move to the folder you choose, then {name} is deleted.
dialog.deleteEmpty: {name} is removed from Aether Mail and from every app connected to this mailbox.
dialog.emptyPermanent: {messages} in {name} will be deleted permanently. This cannot be undone.

list.noFilteredDescription: {folder} has no messages matching the active filters.

reading.noneSelectedDescription: Choose a message from the list to read it here. Press ? to see keyboard shortcuts.
reading.earlierLoadError: This message could not be loaded.

composer.subject: Subject
composer.attachmentLimit: Attachments can total at most 20 files and 20 MB per message.

later.futureError: Choose a time in the future.

invitation.eventUpToDate: Your event is up to date.
invitation.eventRemoved: The event is no longer in your calendar.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.description: Shortcuts work in Mail while you are not typing in a field.
shortcuts.closeOpen: Close the open message or composer

calendar.skipped_one: Skipped {count} event that couldn't be read.
calendar.skipped_other: Skipped {count} events that couldn't be read.

event.viewOnlyDescription: This calendar is shared with you to view only.
event.customRepeatDescription: Custom repeat (edit in the app that created it). Aether can’t save this repeat pattern, so the event is read-only here.
event.repeatingDescription: Changes apply to every occurrence of this repeating event.
event.title: Title
event.everyoneFreeAtTime: Everyone from your organization is free at this time.
event.invitationsSent: Invitations were sent to the attendees.
event.deleteRepeatDescription: This deletes every occurrence of this repeating event, here and in calendar apps synced to Aether.
event.deleteSingleDescription: The event is also removed from calendar apps synced to Aether. This cannot be undone.
event.deleteInvitedNote: The organizer is told you’re not going.
event.deleteAttendeesNote: Attendees are told the event is cancelled.

validation.timesRequired: Choose a start and end time.
validation.endAfterStart: The event must end after it starts.
validation.lastDayAfterFirst: The last day can’t be before the first day.

calendars.title: Calendars
calendars.description: Choose which calendars to show, and share yours with people in your organization.
calendars.deleteDescription: Every event in this calendar is deleted, and people it was shared with lose access. This cannot be undone.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.description: People you write to, also available on your phone over CardDAV, and everyone with a mailbox in your organizations.
contacts.skipped_one: Skipped {count} contact that couldn't be read.
contacts.skipped_other: Skipped {count} contacts that couldn't be read.
contacts.noContactsDescription: Add the people you write to. Contacts you add here also appear in the composer and on synced phones.
contacts.emailAddressesHint: Up to 10. Press Enter or comma after each one.
contacts.deleteDescription: The contact is also removed from phones and apps that sync your contacts. This cannot be undone.
contacts.directoryEmptyDescription: Active mailboxes in your organizations are listed here.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Your account details, language, mail rules, and the app passwords that let mail, calendar and contacts apps connect to your mailboxes.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Your picture shows next to mail you send to people in your organization. If your sign-in provider has a picture, Aether uses it until you upload your own. Your name and email are managed by your administrator or identity provider.
profile.signatureDetailsHint: Filled in when you start a signature from your organization's template.
profile.languageHint: Used for Aether Mail, the admin console, date formatting, and system emails sent to you. Automatic follows your organization’s default language or your browser.
profile.invalidImage: That file isn't a picture that can be read. Choose a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image.
profile.imagePrepareError: The picture could not be prepared.

signatures.title: Signatures
signatures.description: Added to messages you write in Aether Mail. Mail apps on your phone or computer keep their own signature settings.
signatures.emptyDescription: Create one to sign new messages and replies automatically.
signatures.deleteDescription: “{name}” will no longer be added to new messages or replies.

rules.title: Mail rules and automatic replies
rules.description: These run on the mail server as messages arrive, so they apply in Aether Mail and in every other mail client. Rules run in order, after spam filtering.
rules.noMailboxDescription: Rules need a mailbox. Ask an administrator to create one for you.
rules.emptyDescription: Create a rule to file, flag, or mark incoming mail automatically.
rules.dialogDescription: Text matching ignores letter case. Forwarded mail is sent from this mailbox’s address, so delivery failures come back here.
rules.notToMeHint: This mailbox isn’t in To or Cc
rules.deletePermanentlyHint: Discard matching messages as they arrive, without moving them to Trash.
rules.deleteWarning: Messages this rule deletes can’t be recovered. To keep a way back, move them to Trash instead.
rules.forwardToHint: Up to 5 addresses. Replies from the recipients go to the original sender.
rules.keepCopy: Keep a copy in this mailbox
rules.stopProcessingHint: Later rules are skipped for messages this rule matches.
rules.deleteDescription: Messages that arrive from now on are no longer handled by this rule. Messages it already moved stay where they are.

summary.notToMe: this mailbox isn’t in To or Cc
summary.forwardWithoutCopy: forward to {addresses} without keeping a copy

validation.headerRequired: Enter a header name such as List-Id.
validation.sizeRange: Enter a size from 1 KB to 1 GB (1,048,576 KB).

autoReply.title: Automatic replies
autoReply.description: Each sender gets the reply at most once a day. Mailing lists and automated messages never get one.
autoReply.fromHint: Optional. Leave empty to start now.
autoReply.untilHint: Optional. The last day replies are sent.
autoReply.subject: Subject
autoReply.messageRequired: Write the reply people will receive.
autoReply.endBeforeStart: The end date is before the start date.

lists.title: Lists you manage
lists.description: You own these distribution lists, so you can add and remove their members. An administrator manages who can send to them.
lists.membersHint: Mailboxes, other lists or outside addresses. Press Enter or type a comma after each one.

import.title: Import mail
import.description: Copy every folder from another provider into this mailbox over IMAP. Messages that are already here are skipped, so you can run an import again.
import.emptyDescription: Bring over the mail from your old address.
import.interruptedNote: Aether restarted during the import. Start it again; messages already copied are skipped.
import.dialogDescription: Aether signs in to the other account over IMAP and copies its folders. It only reads from the other account and never changes or deletes anything there.
import.startedDescription: You can leave this page. Aether keeps copying in the background.
import.appPasswordNote: Gmail, iCloud and Yahoo need an app password from their account settings, not your normal password. Aether uses it only for this import and does not store it.

validation.hostRequired: Enter the IMAP server, such as imap.gmail.com.
validation.usernameRequired: Enter the username, usually the full address.
validation.passwordRequired: Enter the password or app password.

appPasswords.title: App passwords
appPasswords.description: Use an app password instead of your sign-in password in IMAP and SMTP mail clients. Each one works for a single mailbox. Shared mailboxes appear in your mail app automatically under Shared; they never need their own password.
appPasswords.emptyDescription: Create one to connect a desktop or phone mail client.
appPasswords.createdDescription: Copy the password now. Aether shows it only once.
appPasswords.createDescription: The password is generated for you and shown once.
appPasswords.appleDescription: Download a configuration profile that adds mail, calendar and contacts to an iPhone, iPad or Mac. It contains a new app password, which you can revoke here.
appPasswords.profileDownloadedDescription: Open it on your iPhone, iPad or Mac to install it.
appPasswords.revokeDescription: Mail clients using “{name}” stop connecting immediately. This cannot be undone.
appPasswords.authNote: Authentication: normal password. Use the full mailbox address as the username for both servers.

validation.nameRequired: Name the device or client, for example “Laptop Thunderbird”.

calendarApps.title: Calendar and contacts apps
calendarApps.description: Your Aether calendar and contacts sync to phone and desktop apps over CalDAV and CardDAV. These apps need an app password, not the password you use to sign in on the web.
calendarApps.appPasswordForMailbox: An app password for that mailbox.
calendarApps.enterSettingsAbove: Enter the server address, username and app password above.
calendarApps.iphoneSteps: In Settings, open the accounts list for Calendar, choose Add Account, then Other. Add a CalDAV account for your calendar and a CardDAV account for your contacts.
calendarApps.macSteps: In System Settings, open Internet Accounts, then Add Other Account. Add a CalDAV account and a CardDAV account.
calendarApps.thunderbirdSteps: For the calendar, choose New Calendar, then On the Network. For contacts, choose New Address Book, then Add CardDAV Address Book.
calendarApps.androidSteps: Add an account and choose Login with URL and user name, then pick the calendar and address book to sync.

admin.title: Administration
admin.description: Domains, mailboxes and access for the organizations you manage.
admin.nothingDescription: You are not an owner or administrator of any organization.
admin.noOrgsDescription: Create an organization to add domains and mailboxes.
admin.newOrgDescription: Organizations own domains, mailboxes and members.
admin.slugHint: Used in URLs and identity provider mappings. Lowercase, for example “scala-studios”.
admin.defaultLanguageHint: Used on the sign-in page, in Aether Mail, and for system emails when a person hasn’t chosen a personal language.

validation.orgSlugInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.

general.title: Organization settings
general.description: Identity and language defaults for this organization.
general.languageSectionDescription: Applied for people in this organization who haven’t set a personal language, on branded sign-in pages, and in system emails sent to mailboxes in this organization.

domains.title: Domains
domains.description: Aether receives and sends mail for these domains once their DNS records are in place.
domains.emptyDescription: Add a domain to start creating mailboxes on it.
domains.addDescription: After adding it, publish the DNS records Aether lists for it.
domains.domainInvalid: Enter a domain name such as example.com.
domains.verifiedDescription: Keep these records published so mail is delivered and passes SPF, DKIM and DMARC checks.
domains.unverifiedDescription: Publish the ownership TXT record, wait for DNS to update, then select Verify. Lookups can take a few minutes to reflect changes.
domains.noRecords: No DNS records are required for this domain.
domains.deleteDescription: This deletes the domain and its aliases. A domain that still has mailboxes, active or not, cannot be deleted: delete those mailboxes first. Stored mail stays on disk until an operator removes it.

dmarc.title: DMARC reports
dmarc.descriptionBefore: Aggregate reports receivers sent about mail from
dmarc.emptyDescription: Receivers usually send them once a day after the DMARC record includes rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@{domain}.

mailboxes.title: Mailboxes
mailboxes.description: User mailboxes have an owner account that signs in with the address. Shared mailboxes have members instead.
mailboxes.emptyDescription: Create a mailbox on one of this organization's domains.
mailboxes.createSharedDescription: A shared mailbox has no sign-in. Add members after creating it.
mailboxes.createUserDescription: Aether creates or links an owner account with the mailbox address.
mailboxes.displayNameHint: Shown as the sender name. Optional.
mailboxes.passwordHint: Optional web sign-in password for the owner, at least 12 characters, or empty for single sign-on.
mailboxes.deleteDescription: The mailbox stops receiving mail immediately and its app passwords stop working. Stored mail stays on disk until an operator removes it.
mailboxes.convertToUserDescription: If the address had an owner account before, it is restored as the owner. Members keep their access as delegates but lose the shared folders in their mail apps.
mailboxes.convertToSharedDescription: The owner account stops signing in and its sessions end. Every app password for this mailbox stops working. Mail stays in place and members you add can open it.

delegates.sharedDescription: Full access lets a member read, organize and file mail. Send as and Send on behalf are separate: Send as sends from this address; Send on behalf shows the member's name as the sender.
delegates.userDescription: Full access lets a delegate read and organize this mailbox; Send as additionally allows sending from the address and creating app passwords for it. Read only allows reading in Aether Mail and nothing else.
delegates.emailHint: The email of an active person in this organization.
delegates.removeSharedDescription: They lose access to {address} in Aether Mail and in their mail apps right away.
delegates.removeUserDescription: They lose access to {address}, and the app passwords they created for it stop working.

validation.localPartInvalid: Use letters, digits, dots, hyphens, plus signs or underscores.
validation.passwordMin: Use at least 12 characters, or leave it empty.
validation.quotaInvalid: Enter a whole number of megabytes.

aliases.title: Aliases
aliases.description: Forward mail for an address to up to 100 destinations. Every mailbox among them can send as the alias. A catch-all receives mail for addresses that have no mailbox or alias.
aliases.emptyDescription: Create an alias to forward an address without a separate mailbox.
aliases.listsDescription: One address for a group of up to 5,000 people, listed in the directory. Choose who can send to it, who can send as it, and who can change its members without being an administrator.
aliases.emptyListsDescription: Create a list such as staff@ to reach a group, and decide who is allowed to write to it.
aliases.aliasHint: Forwards to up to 100 addresses. Every mailbox among them can send as the alias.
aliases.listHint: Up to 5,000 members. You choose who can send to the list and who can send as it.
aliases.nameHint: Optional. Shown in the directory and in address suggestions.
aliases.membersHint: Mailboxes, other lists or outside addresses. Press Enter or type a comma after each one.
aliases.destinationsHint: Press Enter or type a comma after each address.
aliases.activeHint: Turn it off to stop forwarding mail without deleting it.
aliases.whoCanSendToList: Who can send to the list
aliases.allowedSendersHint: Addresses, or @example.com for everyone at a domain.
aliases.canSendAsHint: Mailboxes in this organization that can send from the list’s address. Members can’t unless you add them here.
aliases.ownersHint: People in this organization who can add and remove members from their settings, without being administrators.
aliases.deleteDescription: Mail to {label} stops being forwarded immediately.
aliases.ownerNotMember_one: {addresses} isn’t a member of this organization. Add them under Members first.
aliases.ownerNotMember_other: {addresses} aren’t members of this organization. Add them under Members first.

senders.organizationHint: Only people signed in to send from this organization’s domains. Mail from anyone else is rejected.
senders.membersHint: Only the list’s members. Mail from anyone else is rejected.
senders.allowlistHint: Only the addresses and domains below. Mail from anyone else is rejected.

validation.localPartInvalid: Use letters, digits, dots, hyphens, plus signs or underscores.
validation.aliasMax: An alias forwards to up to 100 addresses. Make it a distribution list for more.
validation.listMax: A list can have up to 5,000 members.
validation.listLocalPartRequired: Enter the list’s address. Only an alias can be a catch-all.
validation.allowedSendersRequired: Add at least one address or @domain.

members.title: Members
members.description: People with access to this organization. Only owners can grant or change the owner role.
members.emptyDescription: Add someone who already has an Aether account.
members.addDescription: The person needs an existing Aether account.
members.unknownUser: No Aether account uses this email. Create a mailbox for it, or ask the person to sign in once with single sign-on.
members.suspendDescription: They are signed out everywhere, cannot sign in, and their app passwords stop working for IMAP and SMTP. This applies in every organization they belong to. Mail keeps arriving in their mailboxes.
members.removeDescription: They lose their role here, their delegated access to this organization’s mailboxes, and ownership of its distribution lists. Their account and the mailboxes they own aren’t deleted.

branding.nameAndLogoDescription: Shown instead of Aether's in the app header, the browser tab and on the sign-in page, for everyone in this organization.
branding.nameHint: Leave empty to use the organization name, “{orgName}”.
branding.imageRequirements: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 256 KB and 2048 by 2048 pixels each. Logos fit within 80 by 32 pixels in the sidebar and 240 by 48 on the sign-in page, and one logo is used for both themes until you add the other. The light theme logo also goes into signatures made from the organization template. Use a square image for the favicon.
branding.signInMessageDescription: Replaces the default sign-in prompt when the sign-in page is opened on one of this organization's domains.
branding.messageHint: {count} of 500 characters. Plain text; line breaks are kept.
branding.messagePlaceholder: Sign in with your work account. Locked out? Call the IT desk on extension 4000.
branding.colorsDescription: Each theme has its own colours. Tints and the text on accent buttons follow the accent; hover the buttons in the preview to check the hover and pressed colours.
branding.invalidHex: Enter each colour as a six-digit hex value, such as #fa7e26.
branding.customCssDescription: Added after Aether's styles on the sign-in page, Mail, Calendar, Contacts and Settings, for what the colours don't cover. Administration keeps Aether's styles, so a broken stylesheet can't lock you out of fixing it.
branding.customCssDisabledBefore: Custom CSS is turned off on this server, so the stylesheet below isn't applied. You can still edit it. The operator turns it back on by removing
branding.stylesheetHint: {size} of 32 KB. url() can only point at files on this server, and @import isn't allowed. Every change is recorded in the audit log.

signatures.title: Signature template
signatures.description: People start their signature from this template in Settings → Signatures, with their own name, job title and phone filled in.
signatures.revertedToast: @{domain} uses the template for all domains again
signatures.inheritsNotice: @{domain} uses the template for all domains. Saving here gives it a template of its own.
signatures.conditionalHintAfter: to leave it out when the value is empty.
signatures.logoWidthHint: In pixels. The logo is the light theme logo from Branding, when there is one.
signatures.linksHint: Shown where the template has {{links}}, separated by dots. Up to 10.
signatures.addMailboxPreview: Add a mailbox to preview the template with real details.
signatures.addMailboxDomainPreview: Add a mailbox on @{domain} to preview the template with real details.
signatures.useAllDomains: Use the template for all domains

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Changes and sign-ins in this organization, newest first.
audit.emptyDescription: Actions such as creating mailboxes or verifying domains are recorded here.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.description: A key acts as an administrator of this organization, limited to its scopes. Send it as a bearer token.
apiKeys.emptyDescription: Create a key to manage domains, mailboxes and aliases from scripts.
apiKeys.createdDescription: Copy this token now. You won't be able to see it again.
apiKeys.createDescription: A write scope includes read access.
apiKeys.expiresHint: Optional. The key stops working at the end of this day.
apiKeys.revokeDescription: Requests using “{name}” are rejected immediately. This cannot be undone.

resources.domainsDescription: Domains, DNS records, verification, DMARC reports and each domain’s default quota.
resources.mailboxesDescription: Mailboxes, the organization’s default quota, delegates, mail rules, automatic replies and signatures. Write also imports calendars and contacts for the mailbox owner.
resources.aliasesDescription: Aliases and distribution lists, with their members, sender restrictions and owners.
resources.membersDescription: Members and their roles. Write also adds and removes members.
resources.reportsDescription: Mailbox sizes, last sign-in, inactive mailboxes, top senders and receivers, and mail volume reports. Write also refreshes sizes.
resources.webhooksDescription: Webhooks, their delivery history and test deliveries.
resources.contactsDescription: Organization contacts shown in the directory.
resources.message-traceDescription: Search and export delivery records for the organization’s domains.
resources.sendersDescription: Allowed and blocked senders for the organization and its domains.
resources.mailflowDescription: Mail flow rules, their recent matches and held messages. Write also approves and rejects held messages.
resources.suppressionsDescription: Addresses Aether refuses to send to. Write also adds and removes addresses.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Aether posts matching audit events to these URLs as JSON. Verify the Aether-Signature header with your secret.
webhooks.emptyDescription: Create a webhook to receive events such as mailbox.create or domain.verify.
webhooks.createdDescription: Copy this secret now. You won't be able to see it again.
webhooks.createDescription: Aether signs each request with a secret shown after you create the webhook.
webhooks.eventsHint: Comma-separated audit actions, for example mailbox.create, domain.verify.
webhooks.testQueuedToast: Test event queued. Aether sends it within 15 seconds.
webhooks.deleteDescription: Aether stops sending events to {url} and deletes its delivery history.
webhooks.deliveriesDescription: The 50 most recent deliveries to {url}, newest first.
webhooks.noDeliveriesDescription: Send a test event to check that your endpoint responds.

validation.urlInvalid: Enter a full URL such as https://example.com/aether.
validation.eventsRequired: Enter at least one event name.

identity.title: Identity providers
identity.description: Let people sign in with an OpenID Connect provider. Halo is the recommended provider for Scala Studios installations.
identity.emptyDescription: Connect Halo or another OpenID Connect provider to enable single sign-on.
identity.deleteDescription: People who sign in through this provider can no longer sign in with it. Their accounts and mailboxes are kept.
identity.genericDescription: Any OpenID Connect provider that supports the authorization code flow.
identity.haloIssuerHint: The base URL of your Halo installation.
identity.keepSecretHint: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
identity.webhookSecretHint: Optional. Lets the provider suspend, restore, and sign out users in Aether. In Halo, add a webhook for user.suspend, user.restore, scim.user.*, and session.revoke that points at the URL below, then paste its secret here.
identity.enabledHint: Show this provider on the sign-in page.

scim.title: SCIM provisioning for {name}
scim.description: Let the provider create, update and deactivate Aether accounts. Accounts it creates get a mailbox when their address is on a verified domain, and they can sign in through the provider straight away.
scim.copyOnceNote: Copy the token now. Aether shows it only once. In Halo, paste both into the application's provisioning settings.
scim.enabledNote: SCIM is on. Creating a new token replaces the current one, so update it in the provider at the same time.
scim.disabledNote: Turning SCIM on creates a bearer token for the provider.

discovery.step1: Create an application with the type Web.
discovery.step4: Copy the client ID and secret Halo shows, then continue.

provisioning.autoProvisionHint: When off, only people who already have an Aether account or mailbox can sign in.
provisioning.adminGroupHint: Members of this group become platform administrators. Leave empty to grant nobody.
provisioning.groupMappingsHint: Members of a group join the organization with the chosen role when they sign in.

validation.issuerInvalid: Enter the issuer URL, for example https://halo.example.com.
validation.nameRequired: Enter the name shown on the sign-in button.
validation.slugInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
validation.scopesRequired: Enter at least the openid scope.
